: SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

SELECTION DE CONSULTANTS PAR LES EMPRUNTEURS DE LA BANQUE MONDIALE

REPUBLIQUE ISLAMIQUE DE MAURITANIE

Ministère de l’Energie et du Pétrole

Projet de Développement des Ressources Energétiques et appui au Secteur Minier (DREAM 1)-UGP-MEP

Intitulé de la mission : Recrutement d’un cabinet de conseil pour la réalisation d’une étude de faisabilité relative à la construction d’un complexe industriel d’engrais et de pétrochimie dans la zone de N’Diago

Financement : IDA-Banque Mondiale/ ID : IDA 77310

No. de référence (selon le Plan de Passation des marchés): 01

1. La Mauritanie dispose d’un grand potentiel d’hydrogène bas carbone à base de ressources d’énergie solaires et éoliennes estimées à 4000 GW dont 10% est exploitable dans l’immédiat.

Ces réserves énergétiques s’ajoutent aux champs de gaz à grande réserves  qui sont exploitables à de faibles niveaux d’émissions en carbone. Le pays dispose également d’énormes réserves minières notamment de phosphate, de fer, de cuivre et d’or qui ont été prouvées ainsi que d’autres importantes réserves en minéraux essentiels à la transition énergétique identifiés, tels que le nickel, le cobalt et le lithium.

Ces potentiels constituent de grandes opportunités de développement durable pour le pays. Pour aider la Mauritanie à tirer profit de ces opportunités, la Banque mondiale s’est engagée à financer une série de projets, intitulées « Projet de Développement des Ressources Energétiques et appui au Secteur Minier (DREAM) ».

L’objectif de développement de ce projet est de favoriser les investissements dans l’hydrogène vert et les ressources minérales et d’accroître la fiabilité et l’intégration des énergies renouvelables du réseau électrique national.

2. Dans ce cadre, le groupe de la Banque mondiale a accordé au Gouvernement de la Mauritanie une avance pour la préparation de la phase 1 (DREAM 1). Le Gouvernement de Mauritanie a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : Recrutement d’un cabinet de conseil pour la réalisation d’une étude de faisabilité relative à la construction d’un complexe industriel d’engrais et de pétrochimie dans la zone de N’Diago

3. Le travail du Consultant comprendra notamment les activités et tâches suivantes :

  1. Analyse documentaire et benchmarks
    • Examiner et analyser les études existantes réalisées en Mauritanie, notamment :

            •   Gas Master Plan ;

            •   Plans et perspectives de développement des champs gaziers ;

•   Études de valorisation des minerais, notamment du phosphate ;

            •   Plans et perspectives de développement des champs gaziers ;

            •   Études et stratégies relatives aux énergies renouvelables ;

•   Etudes et documents de planification industrielle, portuaire et d’aménagement du territoire.

  • Réaliser des benchmarks régionaux et internationaux pertinents, incluant :

            •   Complexes industriels, pétrochimiques et d’engrais intégrés ;

            •   Zones industrielles comparables, notamment portuaires ;

            •   Projets combinant gaz naturel et mines (en particulier phosphate), et notamment

                 ceux intégrant les énergies vertes ;

            •   Modèles de partenariats, de gouvernance et de financement réussis pour de tels projets.

2.

  1. Etude technique
    •    Analyse des ressources disponibles intrants pour le complexe (gaz, phosphate, etc) ;
    •    Identification des chaînes de valeur industrielles possibles, notamment pour le méthanol, ammoniac, urée, engrais phosphatés, engrais azotés, polyéthylène, etc. ;
    •    Définition des capacités de production optimales ;
    •    Évaluation des technologies disponibles et de leur maturité et adaptabilité locale ;
    •    Analyse des besoins en infrastructures et utilités de soutien :

            •   Port (y compris extension du port de Ndiago si nécessaire), route et logistique

diverses (bases de vie, bases logistiques, etc.) ;

            •   Transport produits et intrants (routes, pipelines, camions citernes, convoyeurs, etc.)

            •   Énergies (gaz, solaire, éolien, hybridation) ;

            •   Eau (potable, industrielle et dessalement) ;

    •     Indentification et évaluation des sites potentiels pour le complexe et recommandation du site optimal ;
    •     Proposition d’un layout conceptuel de la zone industrielle intégrée, avec ses composantes et phasage éventuel.
    •  
    • 3. Étude de marché et commerciale
      •    Analyse de la demande locale, régionale et internationale pour les produits envisagés ;
      •    Analyse de la concurrence et du positionnement de la Mauritanie ;
      •    Étude des prix, tendances et perspectives de marché  ;
      •    Identification des marchés cibles prioritaires ;
      •    Évaluation des avantages compétitifs (coûts énergie, logistique, fiscalité, carbone).
      •  
      • 4.Analyse préliminaire environnementale et sociale
        •    Identification des enjeux environnementaux et sociaux majeurs liés au site et au complexe ;
        •    Analyse des contraintes réglementaires nationales et internationales ;
        •    Évaluation préliminaire de l’empreinte carbone et du potentiel de réduction via les énergies vertes, par composante du projet ;
        •    Recommandations pour une approche durable et inclusive pour chaque composante du projet.
        •  
        • 5.Étude institutionnelle, juridique et réglementaire
          •    Analyse du cadre institutionnel et réglementaire applicable ;
          •    Identification des autorisations et permis requis ;
          •    Évaluation des incitations existantes et envisageables (fiscales, douanières, etc.) ;
          •    Évaluation des options de partenariats, de gouvernance et de financement réussis ;
          •    Proposition d’un modèle juridico-financier adapté au contexte mauritanien et attractif pour les investisseurs tout en soulignant les débouchés financiers et fiscaux pour l’Etat et les communautés locales ainsi que les populations ;

  Proposition d’un schéma institutionnel de partenariat et de gouvernance de la zone industrielle ;

Pour plus des détails sur les objectifs de la mission voire les termes de références sur le lien ci-dessous.

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1C78XtKsLG5_Xl0pgGZqDUs9I8ExdC6kP/view?usp=sharing

4. Il est prévu que les prestations s’étaleront sur une période de Six (6) à Huit (8) mois.

5. Les Cabinets intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et les expériences pertinentes pour exécuter la mission. Les candidatures seront évaluées suivant la grille d'analyse ci -dessous :

  • Expérience avérée en stratégie Gas-to-Industry en général

20
  • Une expérience internationale confirmée dans les études de faisabilité de projets industriels engrais

25
  • Une expérience internationale confirmée dans les études de faisabilité de projets industriels de pétrochimie

25
  • Une expérience internationale confirmée dans les études de faisabilité de projets industriels intégrés d’engrais et de pétrochimie

30

6. L’Unité de Gestion du DREAM 1 UGP-MEP invite les firmes de consultants (« Consultants ») intéressées à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus.

7. Le Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût (SFQC), telle que décrite dans les procédures de passation des marchés de la Banque Mondiale (Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant de la Banque mondiale le financement de projets d’Investissements - Juillet 2016 révisé en Novembre 2017, Août 2018 et septembre 2023.

8. Il est porté à l’attention des firmes de  Consultants que les dispositions du paragraphe 3.16 des « Règle de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projet d’Investissement (FPI) : Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants et Services de Consultants » [Juillet 2016 révisé en Novembre 2017, Août 2018 et Septembre 2023, Banque mondiale], relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts sont applicables. La Banque Mondiale exige que les entreprises et les personnes physiques qui participent à la passation des marchés dans ses opérations de FPI n’aient pas de conflit d’intérêts.

9. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer avec d’autres firmes pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives sous la forme d’un groupement solidaire ou d’un accord de sous-traitant. Si le candidat est un groupement, il doit inclure dans son dossier de candidature, soit une copie de l’accord de Groupement liant tous les membres du Groupement, soit une lettre d’intention de constituer un tel Groupement signée par tous les membres du Groupement et assortie d’un projet d’accord. Les références des membres d’un groupement seront consolidées lors de l’évaluation des manifestations d’intérêt si l’accord de groupement indique que les membres seront conjointement et solidairement engagés vis-à-vis du client pour réaliser la mission au cas où leur groupement serait retenu.

10. Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires auprès du DREAM, e-mail :  projet@dream.mr  en mettant en copie Monsieur le Coordonnateur du projet, e-mail : a.elkharrachi@dream.mr  Tel : (222) 44 59 59 16, aux heures suivantes : de 9 h à 17 h du lundi au jeudi et de 9 h à 12 h le vendredi

11. Les manifestations d’intérêts doivent comprendre ce qui suit :

  • Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt adressée à Monsieur le Président de la Commission de Passation des Marchés Publics du Ministère de l’Energie et du Pétrole ;
  • Un tableau présentant les références générales et spécifiques attestées (pertinentes pour la Mission) ainsi que toutes informations et documents attestés nécessaires pour les besoins de la grille d’évaluation ci-dessus.

Pour chaque référence - mission, ledit tableau doit préciser :

  • Le bénéficiaire de la mission ;
  • La période de réalisation de la mission ;
  • Une présentation sommaire de la mission.

Le Consultant doit fournir également une copie du Registre de commerce dans son pays d’établissement.

12. Les manifestations d’intérêt doivent être adressées à Monsieur le Président de la Commission de Passation des Marchés Publics du Ministère de l’Energie et du Pétrole par courrier postal à l’adresse de la CPMP : Tevragh-Zeina Ilot K extension lot 0°768 sur la route qui mène à l'hôtel CASA BLU ou par courrier électronique à l’Adresse E-mail : cpmp.mpme@gmail.com, au plus tard le lundi 09 mars 2026 à 12 Heures 00 GMT.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
CONSULTANT SELECTION BY WORLD BANK BORROWERS

ISLAMIC REPUBLIC OF MAURITANIA

Ministry of Energy and Petroleum

Energy Resources Development and Mining Sector Support Project (DREAM 1)

Assignment Title: Recruitment of a consulting firm to conduct a feasibility study for the construction of an industrial fertilizer and petrochemical complex in the N’Diago area

Financing: IDA–World Bank / ID: IDA 77310

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): 01

1. Background

Mauritania has significant low-carbon hydrogen potential based on solar and wind energy resources estimated at 4,000 GW, of which 10% is immediately exploitable.

These energy reserves are complemented by large gas fields that can be exploited at low carbon emission levels. The country also possesses substantial proven mineral reserves, particularly phosphate, iron, copper, and gold, as well as other significant reserves of minerals critical to the energy transition, such as nickel, cobalt, and lithium.

These resources represent major sustainable development opportunities for the country. To help Mauritania capitalize on these opportunities, the World Bank has committed to financing a series of projects entitled the Energy Resources Development and Mining Sector Support Project (DREAM).

The development objective of the project is to promote investment in green hydrogen and mineral resources and to enhance the reliability and integration of renewable energy into the national electricity grid.

2. In this context, the World Bank Group has granted the Government of Mauritania an advance for the preparation of Phase 1 (DREAM 1). The Government intends to use part of this financing to make payments under the following contract:

Recruitment of a consulting firm to conduct a feasibility study for the construction of an industrial fertilizer and petrochemical complex in the N’Diago area.

3. Scope of Services

The Consultant’s work will include, but not be limited to, the following activities:

  1. Desk Review and Benchmarking
  • Review and analyze existing studies carried out in Mauritania, including:
    • Gas Master Plan;
    • Gas field development plans and outlook;
    • Minerals exploitation studies, particularly phosphate;
    • Renewable energy studies and strategies;
    • Industrial, port, and land-use planning documents.
  • Conduct relevant regional and international benchmarks, including:
    • Integrated industrial, petrochemical and fertilizer complexes;
    • Comparable industrial zones, particularly port-based zones;
    • Projects combining natural gas and mining (especially phosphate), including those integrating green energy;
    • Successful partnership, governance, and financing models for such projects.
    •  
    • 2.Technical Study
  • Analysis of available input resources for the complex (gas, phosphate, etc.);
  • Identification of possible industrial value chains, particularly methanol, ammonia, urea, phosphate fertilizers, nitrogen fertilizers, polyethylene, etc.;
  • Definition of optimal production capacities;
  • Assessment of available technologies, their maturity, and local adaptability;
  • Analysis of required supporting infrastructure and utilities, including:
    • Port infrastructure (including potential extension of the N’Diago port), roads, and logistics (accommodation camps, logistics bases, etc.);
    • Transport of products and inputs (roads, pipelines, tanker trucks, conveyors, etc.);
    • Energy (gas, solar, wind, hybrid solutions);
    • Water (potable, industrial, desalination);
  • Identification and assessment of potential sites and recommendation of the optimal site;
  • Proposal of a conceptual layout for the integrated industrial zone, including its components and possible phasing.

          3. Market and Commercial Study

  • Analysis of local, regional, and international demand for the proposed products;
  • Competitive analysis and Mauritania’s positioning;
  • Price analysis, trends, and market outlook;
  • Identification of priority target markets;
  • Assessment of competitive advantages (energy costs, logistics, taxation, carbon footprint).

    4. Preliminary Environmental and Social Analysis

  • Identification of key environmental and social issues related to the site and complex;
  • Analysis of national and international regulatory constraints;
  • Preliminary assessment of carbon footprint and reduction potential through green energy, by project component;
  • Recommendations for a sustainable and inclusive approach for each project component.
  •  
  •     5. Institutional, Legal, and Regulatory Study
  • Analysis of the applicable institutional and regulatory framework;
  • Identification of required authorizations and permits;
  • Assessment of existing and potential incentives (tax, customs, etc.);
  • Evaluation of partnership, governance, and financing options;
  • Proposal of a legal and financial model adapted to the Mauritanian context and attractive to investors, highlighting fiscal and financial benefits for the State, local communities, and populations;
  • Proposal of an institutional partnership and governance framework for the industrial zone.

Further details on the mission objectives are available in the Terms of Reference at the link below:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1C78XtKsLG5_Xl0pgGZqDUs9I8ExdC6kP/view?usp=sharing

4. Duration

The services are expected to be carried out over a period of six (6) to eight (8) months.

5. Qualifications and Evaluation Criteria

Interested consultant firms must provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the assignment. Applications will be evaluated according to the criteria below:

  • Proven experience in Gas-to-Industry strategy in general

20
  • Demonstrated international experience in feasibility studies of fertilizer industrial projects

25
  • Demonstrated international experience in feasibility studies of petrochemical industrial projects

25
  • Demonstrated international experience in feasibility studies of integrated fertilizer and petrochemical projects

30

 (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the services described above.

7. Selection Method

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, and September 2023).

8. Conflict of Interest

Consulting firms are advised that the provisions of paragraph 3.16 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, and September 2023) regarding conflict of interest apply. The World Bank requires that firms and individuals participating in its IPF procurement processes have no conflict of interest.

9. Association of Firms

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications in the form of a joint venture or a subcontracting arrangement. If the applicant is a joint venture, it must include in its application either:

  • A copy of the Joint Venture Agreement binding all members; or
  • A letter of intent to form such a joint venture signed by all members and accompanied by a draft agreement.

The references of joint venture members will be combined during evaluation provided that the joint venture agreement states that members shall be jointly and severally liable to the Client if awarded the contract.

10. Additional Information

Interested Consultant firms may obtain further information from the DREAM Project at:
Email: projet@dream.mr (copy to the Project Coordinator: a.elkharrachi@dream.mr)
Tel: (222) 44 59 59 16

Office hours: Monday to Thursday from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.

11. Expression of Interest Submission Requirements

Expressions of interest must include:

  • A letter of expression of interest addressed to the Chairman of the Public Procurement Commission of the Ministry of Energy and Petroleum;
  • A table presenting certified general and specific references relevant to the assignment, including all necessary supporting documentation for the evaluation criteria above.

For each reference assignment, the table must specify:

  • The beneficiary/client;
  • The period of implementation;
  • A brief description of the assignment.

The Consultant must also provide a copy of its Commercial Register in his country of establishment

12. Submission Deadline

Data: 13 de fevereiro de 2026

 

 

1. O Governo daa República de Cabo Verde recebeu um financiamento do Banco Mundial para custear o Projecto “Turismo Resiliente e Desenvolvimento da Economia Azul em Cabo verde (P176981)”, e pretende aplicar parte dos fundos para pagamentos ao abrigo do contrato para as Construção do Terminal Marítimo de Passageiros Sal Rei (Boa Vista).

 

2. A agência de implementação, Unidade de Gestão Projetos Especiais (UGPE), convida os Concorrentes elegíveis a apresentarem propostas seladas para execução das Construção do Terminal Marítimo de Passageiros Sal Rei (Boa Vista). Para a execução dos trabalhos, a empresa deverá possuir alvará compatíveis com a globalidade dos trabalhos, atualizado à data de entrega da proposta, conforme a legislação cabo-verdiana em vigor ou equiparável para empresas estrangeiras. O período de construção está previsto para 12 meses a partir da data de consignação. Mais detalhes sobre os requisitos são fornecidos nos Cadernos de Encargos e anexos.

 

3.  O Empreiteiro será selecionado com base no método de seleção Solicitação de Propostas (SDP), de acordo com o Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de operações de IPF, revisto em Fevereiro de 2025, que pode ser encontrado publicado no seguinte website: https://www.worldbank.org/ estando aberto a todos os Concorrentes elegíveis. É da responsabilidade do Concorrente compreender, na íntegra, os procedimentos de aquisições do Banco Mundial.

4. Os Concorrentes elegíveis interessados podem obter mais informações junto de Unidade de Gestão Projectos Especiais e/ou analisar o Documento de Concurso durante o horário de expediente das 08h00 ás 16h00 no endereço abaixo indicado.

 

5. O Documento de Concurso em Português poderá ser obtido por e-mail, mediante solicitação enviada para os endereços constantes do ponto 11 deste anuncio ou, a partir do link seguinte: https://ugpe.gov.cv/projeto/reforco-da-sustentabilidade-resiliencia-e-diversificacao-do-sector-do-turismo-em-cabo-verde

 

Respostas aos esclarecimentos solicitados pelos Concorrentes serão disponibilizadas no link acima, no website, e os Concorrentes serão exclusivamente responsáveis por monitorar o website durante o processo de concurso para todos os esclarecimentos e emendas relacionadas com este concurso.

 

6. As propostas devem ser entregues no endereço abaixo indicado (parágrafo 11) até ou antes do dia 06 de abril de 2026 ás 15h00 (hora local).

 

7. A apresentação de Propostas através de correio eletrónico será permitida. Os interessados devem consultar o SDP para mais detalhes.

 

8. Qualquer proposta entregue fora do prazo estipulado será rejeitada.

 

9. A abertura pública das propostas terá lugar nas instalações da Unidade de Gestão de Projetos Especiais – UGPE (paragrafo 11), no dia 06 de abril de 2026 ás 15h30 (hora local).

procnotices.contact_address: 2nd Floor, MECCNAR Complex, Abuko, Kanifing, The Gambia

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

Project: West Africa Coastal Areas Resilience Investment Project 2

Grant No.: E1400-GM

Procurement Reference: GM-CPCU-470791-CS-CQS

Procurement Category: National and International Firms

Assignment Title: THE PREPARATION OF AN ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT (ESIA) FOR THE KOTU STREAM

    1.  Background

The Gambia’s territories, and particularly the Greater Banjul area, is vulnerable to the effects of climate change, including rising sea levels, increased and erratic rainfall and more extreme weather events. These phenomena increase the risk of flooding and put pressure on existing infrastructure. To address these challenges, sub-projects have been launched that combine structural and non-structural (institutional strengthening for environmental protection) measures, to improve the resilience of local communities and sustainable      management of water resources.

The Government of The Gambia, through the West Africa Coastal Areas (WACA) Resilience Investment Project (ResIP) financed by the World Bank, is preparing interventions along the Kotu Stream to address recurrent fluvial and pluvial flooding. The catchment area of the Stream is approximately 40 km², and flooding has been exacerbated by rapid urbanization, climate change, and inadequate drainage systems. These events have resulted in significant damage to properties, livelihoods, and public infrastructure, while also posing risks to public health and the environment.

The WACA Program is a regional initiative that supports West African countries in strengthening resilience to coastal and riverine flooding, erosion, and climate risks. It promotes sustainable ecosystem-based and infrastructure…. solutions to protect communities, livelihoods, and critical assets. The Gambia’s participation in WACA aims to reduce vulnerability to flooding, improve climate resilience, and enhance socio-economic development through integrated water and coastal management approaches.

Based on the screening and initial scoping conducted by the National Environment Agency (NEA) through its Environmental Impact Assessment Technical Working Group (EIA-TWG), an ESIA Scoping Report was developed in June 2025 to guide the preparation of flood-mitigation infrastructure along the Kotu Stream. The scoping exercise confirmed that the project interventions are likely to generate a range of environmental and social impacts, both positive and adverse, that warrant a detailed Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) in accordance with national regulations and the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs).

The ESIA shall be prepared in a manner that is fully consistent with the laws and regulations of The Gambia specifically, the EIA regulations (2014) under the auspices of the National Environment Agency, and the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs) under the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF). The ESIA will ensure that the proposed interventions are environmentally and socially sustainable, and that risks are adequately mitigated while maximizing project benefits in line with national priorities and WACA’s regional objectives.

    1.      Objectives of the Consultancy

The objective of this assignment is to conduct a detailed Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) study for the Kotu Stream, in consistent and compliant with the relevant national laws and policies of the Government of The Gambia (GoTG) and Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) of the World Bank and taking into consideration the World Bank Group’s Environmental, Health and Safety Guidelines. It will ensure that all positive and adverse impacts associated with sub-project activities will be considered and that the appropriate mitigation measures will be in place. 
 

    1. Scope of Work

The consultancy firm is expected to undertake investigations on social aspects, environmental aspects as well as conservation of natural resources, historical heritages and cultural (if applicable), and public consultations and disclosures. In conducting the tasks described in the scope of work, they will work closely with the Engineering Consultant responsible for the feasibility studies, detailed design and supervision of the Kotu Stream, HYDRO NOVA.

Specific tasks to be undertaken include;

    1.  Firm Profile & Experience

The consulting firm must demonstrates expertise in multidisciplinary environmental and social assessments of water resources, hydrological, and infrastructure projects. With at least 5 similar assignments conducting ESIA for infrastructure/hydraulic/ nature -based projects. Proven experience in stakeholder engagement in urban and peri-urban settings and familiar with World Bank ESF.

    1. Proposed Team Composition

The consultancy firm’s project team shall comprise of the following expertise as minimum:

  • Team Leader / ESIA Specialist – An MSc in Environment Management or Engineering, Project Management at least 10 years’ experience in leading ESIAs for World Bank projects.
  • Hydrologist/Water Resources Engineer – An MSc in Hydrology with 8 years expertise in stream morphology, flood management, Coastal engineering.
  • Ecologist/Biodiversity Expert – A BSc in Ecology with at least 10 years expertise in aquatic and riparian ecosystems.
  • Social Safeguards Expert – A BSc in Development Studies or related field with at least 10 years (or MSc in Development Studies or related field with at least 5 years) of professional work experience in ESIA experience in resettlement, stakeholder engagement, gender/GBV, and social inclusion.
  • Environmental Engineer – MSc in Environmental Science or related field with at least 10 years of professional work experience with infrastructure projects (bridges, culverts, bank protection).
  • Socioeconomic Expert - MA degree in a Social Policy and Development, Gender, Sociology or any other Social Science with at least 7 years of professional work experience with infrastructure projects (bridges, culverts, bank protection).
  • OHS/Community Health & Safety Specialist – MSc degree in occupational health and safety and at least 5 years of professional work experience with infrastructure projects.
  • GIS/Mapping Specialist – MSc degree in GIS, remote sensing and at least 7 years of professional work experience in similar projects.
  1.  Duration of the study: The consultancy is expected to be completed in 3 (THREE) months.

Consulting firms may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture (JV) and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a JV, all the partners in the JV shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. JV Agreement should be included in the EOI.

Firms will be selected in accordance with the Selection Based on “Consultants Qualification Selection” (CQS) Method which is available on the Bank’s website set out in the Procurement Regulations 2025. Only the Most responsive Firm shall be invited to submit Technical and Financial proposals for Negotiation.
